# Independent audit of interval-fiber hinge normality

The proof in `candidate 95c59f781b5c15f4`
passes in its stated d=1, finite positive-interval-fiber scope.

The local continuous signs are fixed at +/-1. Both cap lengths and
the exact full-interval cover margin are continuous piecewise affine
in the remaining ambient coefficients. For opposing signs, minimizing
max(x-p,q-x) at the clipped midpoint gives precisely the claimed
finite affine pieces. Equal signs and endpoint optima are included.

The local error bound is valid. The projection normal cone for a
polyhedron has a nonnegative representation using linearly independent
active rows, after eliminating linear dependences. Their least
singular value bounds the multiplier sum by a fixed multiple of the
projection distance. The finitely many row subsets give a uniform
polyhedral error bound. In a sufficiently small neighborhood only
partition cells containing the feasible reference point occur, so
every cell's feasible subpolyhedron is nonempty and its own cell
constraints have zero violation on that cell.

The nearest feasible points stay near the local minimizer, and the
locally Lipschitz objective therefore admits the displayed exact
penalty with a finite coefficient. Its generalized-gradient condition
has objective coefficient one. The sum-rule inclusions are used in
the valid direction: zero in the penalty gradient yields an element
of the larger sum of compact convex subgradient sets, which is enough
for the multiplier representation. No Slater assumption enters.

The coverage-gradient lift is also correct. Each limiting affine
piece has a dual-optimal interval minimax certificate at the limiting
configuration. Convex combinations remain dual optimal because the
dual objective is concave and bounded above by the primal value.
Any primal minimizer forms a saddle pair with that combined dual
certificate; its positively weighted margins vanish. The a,b
gradients depend only on the weights, so selecting this common actual
contact causes no discrepancy in those gradient equations. Finally,
in d=1 multiplication by u=+/-1 recovers the continuous-moment
equation exactly from the mass and integer-moment equations and the
cap/contact margins. There is no missing tangential rotation condition.

The normality assertion is compatible with the separate exact
counterexample in `candidate 6521ec5aae22f16f`:
normal stresses can exist at every local minimum while none has a
proposed additional source-to-contact convex-order property.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
